Candlemas Crêpes with Butter and Sugar

Served at: Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation)

Makes about 12-14 crêpesPrep 15 min (plus 30 min resting)Cook 25 min

These delicate crêpes are a beloved tradition for Candlemas, or La Chandeleur, celebrated on February 2nd. Their round, golden shape is said to symbolize the sun and the return of longer days after winter, bringing hopes of prosperity for the year ahead. Simple yet elegant, they are traditionally enjoyed with just a sprinkle of sugar and a touch of butter.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (120g) all-purpose flour
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1 tablespoon (13g) granulated sugar
  • 1 1/2 cups (360ml) whole milk
  • 2 tablespoons (28g) unsalted butter, melted, plus more for cooking
  • For serving:
  • Unsalted butter, softened
  • Granulated sugar

Method

  1. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, salt, and 1 tablespoon of granulated sugar.
  2. In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs and milk together until well combined.
  3. Gradually add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients, whisking constantly until the batter is smooth and free of lumps.
  4. Stir in the 2 tablespoons of melted butter.
  5. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and let the batter rest in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours. This allows the flour to fully hydrate, resulting in more tender crêpes.
  6. Heat a 8-inch (20 cm) non-stick crêpe pan or skillet over medium heat. Lightly butter the pan for the first crêpe.
  7. Pour about 1/4 cup (60ml) of batter into the hot pan, immediately tilting and swirling the pan to coat the bottom evenly with a thin layer of batter.
  8. Cook for 1-2 minutes, or until the edges are lightly golden and the crêpe easily lifts from the pan.
  9. Flip the crêpe with a spatula and cook for another 30-60 seconds, until lightly browned on the second side.
  10. Slide the cooked crêpe onto a plate. Repeat with the remaining batter, lightly buttering the pan as needed between crêpes.
  11. To serve, spread a thin layer of softened butter on each warm crêpe, sprinkle generously with granulated sugar, and fold into quarters or roll up.

Tips

  • Ensure your pan is hot enough; a drop of water should sizzle and evaporate quickly. If crêpes are sticking, the pan might not be hot enough or needs more butter.
  • For a richer flavor, you can add 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract or a tablespoon of rum to the batter.
  • Leftover crêpes can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 days, separated by parchment paper, and reheated gently in a pan or microwave.
